steps.note: Start a multi-stage event so an RFQ pricing stage can be configured.
A title is required for a publishable event.
Configure the event as an RFQ, which supports vendor bids and best-price comparison.
Apply the RFQ pricing template before adding line items.
Create a line item whose competing prices can be compared.
Commit a bidding schedule before publishing.
Invite two participating vendors so one can provide the L1 price.
Publish the event so vendors can submit bids.
Confirm the event reached a real published project page.
Confirm the first vendor's bid was accepted.
Confirm the second vendor's bid was accepted.
Open the buyer comparison grid containing the competing bids.
Verify the buyer-side ranking follows the lowest bid.
Verify the buyer-side lower bid is 90 for the second vendor.
Move to the participating vendor's supplier-portal session.
Open the event's RFQ pricing view as the vendor.
Check whether the vendor view exposes a Best Price indicator.
Check for the known L1 value in the vendor's view, although the catalog cannot prove it is the per-line best-price field.
